object: The frozen state-of-health overview defines battery health relative to specification, says capacity and other useful parameters generally deteriorate over time and use, and says evaluation methods and application thresholds vary. The memory-effect overview defines true memory effect for nickel-cadmium rechargeable cells and says lithium-based cells are not normally subject to it, while also noting that rechargeable batteries have finite lives and lose capacity with age. These generic mechanisms make chemistry, age, use, temperature, cycles, capacity, impedance, and charge acceptance relevant, but they do not establish a universal one-year deadline, an exact retention percentage, or a ranking among FOYCOY, Plantronics, Soundcore, and TOZO. The four seller bodies also use different battery wording, including an anomalous lithium-metal field on the rechargeable TOZO listing, so a charging rule or chemistry claim must not be silently transferred across them.
subject: battery-health and chemistry boundary

object: Preserve every community statement as a scoped report. The AirPods thread includes a heavy user reporting battery or sound annoyance around two years, a motorcycle user reporting repeated six-to-eight-month replacements under specific exposure and service conditions, a three-year user reporting reduced battery life but continued use, and an unsupported universal two-to-three-year claim. A different iPhone thread reports cheap wireless knock-offs with only about 2.5 hours per charge but daily use for over a year, separating per-charge runtime from service life. The Moondrop Sparks discussion says the case was not sold separately and contains conflicting claims about whether another case would charge or pair the buds. Models, workloads, sweat, pressure, accidents, support programmes, and jurisdictions differ, and none of these threads estimates population prevalence or ranks the four frozen listings.

object: Audit all four complete frozen seller bodies without treating their wording as independent durability testing. The FOYCOY X10 page displays SKU B09P3Q59J9, $29.99, a 93 percent rating over 12 reviews, up to 6 hours per charge and 40 hours with the case, one lithium-ion battery, and seller troubleshooting text that mentions charging-contact oxidation, earbud-to-earbud pairing, and reset. The renewed Plantronics BackBeat FIT 3100 page displays SKU B07NX25KXB, $59.95, a 60 percent rating over 81 reviews, up to 5 hours plus 10 case hours, model 211855-99-cr, one lithium-polymer battery, and app firmware-update wording. The renewed Soundcore Liberty page displays SKU B07WQSD5QM, $30.99, no reviews, 8 hours per charge and 100 hours with the case, model A3912, and one lithium-polymer battery. The TOZO T12 page displays SKU B08FT8VN57, $39.98, no reviews, over 6 hours per charge and 28 hours with the case, model T12, and a page battery field that says one lithium-metal battery. None of the four bodies supplies a controlled one-year retention curve, failure prevalence, independent same-condition comparison, battery-replacement route, complete warranty and return scope, or proof that a displayed rating predicts longevity.
subject: complete TWS listing matrix

object: A listing can enter the admissible purchase set only if its exact seller and condition, battery and case history, warranty and return, regional service, replacement earbud and case compatibility, firmware and reset path, and same-condition runtime and fault checks are acceptable to the buyer. The FOYCOY rating and troubleshooting body do not prove long-term reliability; the Plantronics and Soundcore routes add renewed-condition and prior-battery uncertainty; the TOZO route adds an inconsistent battery field and no displayed reviews. Because the frozen corpus contains no exact-model longitudinal durability comparison and leaves support routes unresolved, no unique current winner clears the gate. Keeping the current audio setup and deferring is required rather than selecting by rating or advertised case hours.
subject: longevity and support gate

object: A single silent, low-volume, uncharged, or disconnected side is not by itself a battery diagnosis. The FOYCOY seller body says charging-contact oxidation can prevent charging or power-on and says an unpaired pair can leave only one earbud connected, with reset offered as a troubleshooting route. The generic pairing page defines pairing as the initial linkage that enables device communication, and the stereo page describes two independent audio channels, but neither identifies the cause of an exact earbud failure. The wired Sennheiser IE 600 thread reports left and right one-side failures and contains disagreement over cable versus driver causes even though the product is not true wireless. These sources establish multiple symptom categories and the need for diagnosis, not the prevalence or root cause of any captured TWS listing.
subject: one-side symptom and service boundary

object: Before checkout, verify the exact seller and SKU, new or renewed condition, refurbisher and prior battery history where applicable, current price, return window, warranty issuer and duration, regional service eligibility, firmware-update path, reset and re-pair procedure, contact-cleaning guidance, and whether individual earbuds, charging case, or battery service can be obtained and paired to the exact model. Record a same-volume, same-codec, same-feature baseline for single-charge runtime, left and right discharge, charging reliability, reconnects, and dropouts, then repeat under the same conditions across the return period and later checkpoints. For a defensible longevity ranking, obtain exact-model multi-unit or longitudinal evidence that reports usage hours, charge conditions, environment, failure definitions, censoring, replacement handling, and sample size rather than converting seller hours, ratings, or cross-model anecdotes into a failure rate.
